arxiv-2207-01988.title: Unsupervised Crowdsourcing with Accuracy and Cost Guarantees
arxiv-2207-01988.creator: Yashvardhan Didwania, Jayakrishnan Nair, N. Hemachandra
arxiv-2207-01988.description: Abstract We consider the problem of cost-optimal utilization of a crowdsourcing platform for binary, unsupervised classification of a collection of items, given a prescribed error threshold. Workers on the crowdsourcing platform are assumed to be divided into multiple classes, based on their skill, experience, and/or past performance.

arxiv-2210-08006.title: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
arxiv-2210-08006.creator: Honours Programme, Project Report
arxiv-2210-08006.description: Abstract Cloud services are important for societal function such as healthcare, commerce, entertainment and education. Cloud can provide a variety of features such as increased collaboration and inexpensive computing. Failures are unavoidable in cloud services due to the large size and complexity, resulting in decreased reliability and efficiency.

arxiv-2404-15175.title: Using analytic models to describe effective PDFs
arxiv-2404-15175.creator: S. A. Ochoa-Oregon a , D. F. Rentería-Estrada b , R. J. Hernández-Pinto a , G. F. R. Sborlini c , P. Zurita d,e
arxiv-2404-15175.description: Abstract Parton distribution functions play a pivotal role in hadron collider phenomenology. They are non-perturbative quantities extracted from fits to available data, and their scale dependence is dictated by the DGLAP evolution equations. In this article, we discuss machine-assisted strategies to efficiently compute PDFs directly incorporating the scale evolution without the need of separately solving DGLAP equations.

arxiv-2405-19475.title: Detection of Low-Energy Electrons with Transition-Edge Sensors
arxiv-2405-19475.creator: Carlo Pepe, Benedetta Corcione, Francesco Pandolfi, Hobey Garrone, Eugenio Monticone, Ilaria Rago, Gianluca Cavoto, Alice Apponi, Alessandro Ruocco, Federico Malnati, Danilo Serazio, Mauro Rajteri
arxiv-2405-19475.description: Abstract We present the first detection of electrons with kinetic energy in the 100 eV range with transition-edge sensors (TESs). This has been achieved with a ( 100 × 100 ) (100\times 100) μ \upmu m 2 Ti-Au bilayer TES, with a critical temperature of about 84 mK.

arxiv-2410-09186.title: AI Learning Algorithms: Deep Learning, Hybrid Models, and Large-Scale Model Integration
arxiv-2410-09186.creator: Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz, Elias Hossain, Abdoljalil Addeh, Keyan Alexander Rahimi
arxiv-2410-09186.description: Abstract In this paper, we discuss learning algorithms and their importance across various applications, emphasizing their ability to identify key patterns and features in a straightforward, easy-to-understand manner. We review the main concepts of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), and hybrid models.

arxiv-2410-23353.title: On Computational Complexity of Unitary and State Design Properties
arxiv-2410-23353.creator: Yoshifumi Nakata, Yuki Takeuchi, Martin Kliesch, Andrew Darmawan
arxiv-2410-23353.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yoshifumi Nakata, Yuki Takeuchi, Martin Kliesch, Andrew Darmawan. We investigate unitary and state t t -designs from a computational complexity perspective. First, we address the problems of computing frame potentials that characterize (approximate) t t -designs.

arxiv-2505-11881.title: Revisiting Residual Connections: Orthogonal Updates for Stable and Efficient Deep Networks
arxiv-2505-11881.creator: Giyeong Oh Woohyun Cho Siyeol Kim Suhwan Choi Youngjae Yu, Yonsei University, Maum.AI, Seoul National University
arxiv-2505-11881.description: Abstract Residual connections are pivotal for deep neural networks, enabling greater depth by mitigating vanishing gradients. However, in standard residual updates, the module’s output is directly added to the input stream. This can lead to updates that predominantly reinforce or modulate the existing stream direction, potentially underutilizing the module’s capacity for learning entirely novel features.

arxiv-2602-24203.title: Vacancy-induced local moments in quantum paramagnetic phases: An SU( N N ) designer Hamiltonian study
arxiv-2602-24203.creator: Md Zahid Ansari, Souvik Kundu, Kedar Damle
arxiv-2602-24203.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Md Zahid Ansari, Souvik Kundu, Kedar Damle. We explore the effects of non-magnetic impurities (vacancy disorder) on the quantum paramagnetic phases stabilized by SU( N N ) designer Hamiltonians on bipartite lattices. Using the results of our quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that isolated vacancies seed emergent spin S = 1 / 2 S=1/2 moments in their vicinity when the low-temperature state has valence bond solid order.

pmc-10642568.title: The Effects of Mukbang Watching on Enteral Feeding Intolerance Among Critically Ill Patients: Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trail
pmc-10642568.creator: Yao Yin, Chao-Feng Fan
pmc-10642568.description: PurposeWith an estimated prevalence of 38%, enteral feeding intolerance (EFI) is common in critically ill patients receiving enteral nutrition (EN), and is associated with higher mortality and longer duration of mechanical ventilation. Various methods have been reported to decrease the incidence of EFI during EN, such as post-pyloric feeding, continuous EN delivery, abdominal massage, and probiotic supplementation.

pmc-11516648.title: Empowerment and interprofessional collaboration in health promotion centre Murska Sobota
pmc-11516648.creator: A Atalaia, V Fischill-Neudeck, P Betznec, R Gorjan, C Peinhaupt, H-P Wiesinger, W Habacher
pmc-11516648.description: BackgroundHealth promotion centres (HPCs) were introduced in Slovenian primary health care centres to provide interventions against risk factors for noncommunicable diseases (NCDs). HPCs integrate a multidisciplinary and community-based primary care approach to the prevention of NCDs and provide free lifestyle intervention programmes.

pmc-11814461.title: Molecular assessment of splicing variants in a cohort of patients with inborn errors of immunity: methodological approach and interpretation remarks
pmc-11814461.creator: Laura Miguel Berenguel, Carla Gianelli, Elisabet Matas Pérez, Teresa del Rosal, Ana Méndez Echevarría, Ángel Robles Marhuenda, Marta Feito Rodríguez, Maria Teresa Caballero Molina, Lorena Magallares García, Brenda Sánchez Garrido, Samantha Hita Díaz, Luis Allende Martínez, Pilar Nozal Aranda, Carmen
pmc-11814461.description: BackgroundSplicing is the molecular mechanism to produce mature messenger RNA (mRNA) before its translation into protein. It is estimated that 50% of disease-causing mutations disrupt splicing, mostly of them affecting canonical positions. However, variants occurring in coding regions or deep-intronic variants can also affect splicing. In these cases, interpretation of the results may be challenging and molecular validation is required.

pmc-12373723.title: Biotechnological potential of Cannabis sativa adventitious roots for producing immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory bioactive compounds
pmc-12373723.creator: Su Hyun Park, Jeong Moo Han, Yun Hye Kim, Hyeon Jin Lee, Young Bae Ryu, Hyung Won Ryu, Jae Cheol Jeong, Seon Min Oh, Woo Sik Kim
pmc-12373723.description: Cannabis sativa L. (C. sativa), commonly known as hemp, is widely recognized for its diverse range of bioactive compounds with therapeutic potential in medicinal, industrial, and nutritional applications. This study investigates the use of adventitious roots (ARs) derived from C. sativa as a scalable platform for producing bioactive metabolites with immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory properties. We first isolated extracts from C.

pmc-13246952.title: Large Animal Models of Tricuspid Regurgitation: Relevance, Limitations, and Future Directions
pmc-13246952.creator: Talia Sukienik, Kosuke Nakamae, Chihiro Miyagi, Grisha Yelisetty, Syed Faizullah Hussaini, Tatsuya Watanabe, Junya Matsuda, Satoshi Yuhara, Daisuke Onohara
pmc-13246952.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Despite growing interest in tricuspid regurgitation (TR), evidence remains insufficient to define the optimal timing of intervention and therapeutic strategies, highlighting the need for robust experimental models. Existing large animal models of TR use diverse approaches and can be grouped into two categories: direct valvular interventions targeting the tricuspid leaflets, annulus, or chordae, and indirect induction through mechanisms such as increased right ventricular loading, pulmonary hypertension, or pacing-induced tachycardia.

pmc-13378635.title: Mammalian Osteoderm Ultrastructure in the Armored Acomys Spiny Mouse Tail
pmc-13378635.creator: Joseph Deering, Malcolm Maden, Marc D McKee
pmc-13378635.description: The skin of mammals acts as a barrier against pathogens, ultraviolet radiation, and mechanical trauma. Embedded within the dermal tail skin of spiny mice (genus Acomys) lie osteoderms—finely structured, symmetrically patterned, bone‐like armor plates akin to those in armadillos and non‐avian reptiles.

pmc-13395696.title: Becoming, sensibility, and imagination in social research. A collaborative exploration with defenders of water in Chile
pmc-13395696.creator: María Consuelo Sánchez, Hugo Marcelo Zunino, Martin Araneda, Carla Cepeda
pmc-13395696.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In the framework of recent critiques of modern epistemologies that dichotomize sentient human beings from the world, this article explores modes of knowledge grounded in the interconnected becoming of human beings, other living beings, society, and nature. Drawing on the insights of Gilles Deleuze, Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, and Merleau-Ponty, among others, we develop a mode of social inquiry that approaches knowledge as a creative and collective endeavor activated as human beings enter into a sensible and imaginative relationship with the world.

pmc-13537597.title: Coral restoration is only practical when local human pressure levels are low
pmc-13537597.creator: Cole Baird Brookson, Ariel Greiner
pmc-13537597.description: Coral reefs are threatened by interacting local (fishing, coastal development) and global (climate change) stressors that degrade coral cover and reduce overall reef biodiversity. Adding coral to the reef (coral restoration) is gaining prominence as a management strategy, however it is unclear whether restoration alone can ensure self-sustaining high coral cover (i.e., > 30% coral cover) under interacting stressors.

pmc-13664668.creator: Bo Dong, Weijie Zou, Wenqian Hu, Hongxiao Wu, Yaqing Jing, Fuquan Xie, Shuo Zhang, Weiming Lin
pmc-13664668.description: ObjectivesDouble‐antibody sandwich enzyme‐linked immunosorbent assay (DAS‐ELISA) is a simple and accurate method for detecting viral pathogens. This study established a DAS‐ELISA for the diagnosis of feline coronavirus (FCoV).MethodsIn this study, DAS‐ELISA was performed using FCoV S‐protein rabbit polyclonal and mouse monoclonal antibodies. The optimal reaction conditions were determined using the chessboard method.
